key_insight: MSC-LBM removes the acoustic-time-step bottleneck in low-Re transient lattice Boltzmann simulations by defect-correcting the unsplit residual with an exact per-wavenumber macroscopic solve, preserving BDF2 accuracy while accelerating convergence.
engineering_relevance: This enables much faster, time-accurate CFD for low-to-moderate Reynolds-number flows, especially when refinement would otherwise make standard explicit or dual-time LBM prohibitively slow.
method: Defect-correct the unsplit kinetic residual using a macroscopic-shadow correction.
Solve a Stokes-like system exactly for conserved residual moments at each Fourier wavenumber.
Use a BDF2 fixed point; along the TRT axis, the correction targets hydrodynamic slow modes after non-hydrodynamic perturbations are removed.
evidence_signal: Timing campaigns report 27.95× and 52.71× wall-clock speedups at N=256, Re=1, with matched-accuracy gains increasing to 122.02× at N=1024 and remaining effective across Re=10^-4 to 100.
watch_item: The method’s demonstrated regime is limited to low-to-moderate Reynolds-number transients, and performance depends on accurate coarse-solver relinearisation and a Fourier/symbol-based setup that may be less direct for complex geometries.
paper_title: A macroscopic-shadow-corrected lattice Boltzmann method for fast, time-accurate simulation of low-Reynolds-number transient flows
